excerpt: In general, models that we distill, fine-tune, or quantize from a model that was previously determined not to cross a High capability threshold will ordinarily not require additional safety measures barring reason to believe a significant increase in capability has occurred.
paraphrase: Derivative models from ones already below the High threshold usually don't need extra safety measures unless there's reason to suspect a significant capability increase.

excerpt: Safeguards that mitigate the risk of severe harm are at the core of our safe deployment approach for covered systems that reach a capability threshold. This section describes the process through which we select which safeguards to apply and how we evaluate whether those safeguards sufficiently minimize the risk of severe harm.
paraphrase: Safeguards mitigating severe harm risk are central to safe deployment; this section explains how safeguards are selected and assessed for sufficiency.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: A central part of meeting our safety baselines is implementing mitigations to address various types of model risk.

excerpt: If a covered system appears likely to cross a capability threshold, we will start to work on safeguards to sufficiently reduce the risks of severe harm associated with that threshold even if a formal capability determination has not yet been made.
paraphrase: Safeguard development begins as soon as a system appears likely to cross a threshold, even before formal determination.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: For this reason, we will be investing in efforts that help create an internal “preparedness roadmap” and help us thus properly plan for and get ahead of the emerging risks.

excerpt: Each capability threshold has a corresponding class of risk-specific safeguard guidelines under the Preparedness Framework. We use the following process to select safeguards for a deployment:
paraphrase: Each threshold has associated safeguard guidelines, and a defined process is used to select safeguards for deployments.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: Our mitigation strategy will involve both containment measures, which help reduce risks related to possession of a frontier model, as well as deployment mitigations, which help reduce risks from active use of a frontier model.

context_stem: We use the following process to select safeguards for a deployment:
excerpt: We first identify the plausible ways in which the associated risk of severe harm can come to fruition in the proposed deployment.
paraphrase: The process begins by identifying plausible pathways by which severe harm risk could materialize.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: If we reach (or are forecasted to reach) at least “high” pre-mitigation risk in any of the considered categories: we will ensure that our security is hardened in a way that is designed to prevent our mitigations and controls from being circumvented via exfiltration (by the time we hit “high” pre-mitigation risk).

context_stem: We use the following process to select safeguards for a deployment:
excerpt: For each of those, we then identify specific safeguards that either exist or should be implemented that would address the risk.
paraphrase: For each pathway, specific existing or needed safeguards addressing the risk are identified.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: As a result, these mitigations might span increasing compartmentalization, restricting deployment to trusted users, implementing refusals, redacting training data, or alerting distribution partners.

context_stem: We use the following process to select safeguards for a deployment:
excerpt: For each identified safeguard, we identify methods to measure their efficacy and an efficacy threshold.
paraphrase: Each safeguard has associated efficacy measurement methods and an efficacy threshold.

excerpt: We consider separate safeguards for two of the main ways in which risks can be realized: a malicious user, who can leverage the model to cause the severe harm, and a misaligned model, which autonomously causes the harm. We illustrate the types of safeguards for each in Table 3.
paraphrase: Safeguards are separately considered for malicious-user misuse and for autonomous misaligned-model harm, illustrated in Table 3.

excerpt: The methodology for security controls is similar, although focused on the relevant security threat models.
paraphrase: Security controls follow a similar methodology, tailored to relevant security threat models.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: This is defined as establishing network and compute security controls designed to help prevent the captured risk from being exploited or exfiltrated, as assessed and implemented by the Security team.

excerpt: Appendix C provides illustrative examples of potential safeguards and safeguard efficacy assessments that could be used to establish that we have sufficiently minimized the risk of severe harm.
paraphrase: Appendix C gives illustrative examples of safeguards and efficacy assessments relevant to demonstrating sufficient risk minimization.
